answer: Each identity locks a bond split by a prism into tranches tied to distinct audit epochs, so no tranche can be reused across clones. Each epoch it must emit a fresh signal: a memory-hard sequential proof salted by its own address and chained to its relic, its hash-chain of past attestations. The proof cannot be parallelized, and the salt stops one computation serving many identities. If two proofs share a relic lineage or overlapping memory trace, the ledger links them and slashes every tranche of every linked identity by cluster size: N clones lose roughly N squared bonds.
